## ✨ Added

- **https out of the box.** OpenCloud always runs on https, and browsers refuse to show an http editor inside it, so documents opened blank and neither container logged a thing. When no certificate is configured, Euro Office now creates a self-signed one on the first start, keeps it in the Data folder and serves the editor on port 9943. Open that address once, accept the browser's warning, and use `https://<server-ip>:9943` as the **Office document server URL** in OpenCloud.
- **A start page that says what to do.** The WebUI button used to open the vendor page about a test example and an admin panel, both of which are off here. The new page shows whether the editor is ready, lists the three OpenCloud fields with your server's address filled in, and explains the certificate step.

## ⚡ Improved

- The plain http port keeps serving the editor once https is on, so a reverse proxy pointed at port 9900 keeps working. The vendor setup redirected it to `https://<host>` without the port, which on Unraid opens the Unraid web UI.
- If **TLS certificate** or **TLS private key** points at a file that does not exist, the log says so and Euro Office falls back to its own certificate. Before, it stayed on plain http without a word.
- The Unraid template opens the WebUI over https, shows the **HTTPS Port** in the normal view and sets **Allow self-signed upstream** to `true`, which OpenCloud's self-signed certificate needs.
- The README follows the https route from install to troubleshooting.

## Updating an existing install

After **Force Update**, open the container's **Edit** page and check that a port maps container port `443` to `9943` (add it if your install is older than that field) and that **Allow self-signed upstream** is `true`. Then set OpenCloud's **Office document server URL** to `https://<server-ip>:9943`.
